title: From Prejudice to Parity: A New Approach to Debiasing Large Language Model Word Embeddings
findings: The proposed debiasing method, DeepSoftDebias, was found to be effective at reducing religious bias in large language model word embeddings. For religion, the method achieved an average increase of 0.61 in Mean Average Cosine (MAC) similarity, moving scores closer to the ideal unbiased value of 1.0. On the StereoSet and CrowS-Pairs datasets, the method also produced scores close to the ideal 50, indicating a significant reduction in stereotypes. While downstream task performance was largely unaffected, a small performance decrease (-0.037 F1 score) was noted for religion-debiased embeddings on sentence-pair tasks.

measurement_description: Stereotypical bias associated with religious groups. The evaluation involved measuring the change in bias metrics (Stereotype Score, Crows Metric Score, Mean Average Cosine Similarity) on datasets like StereoSet and CrowS-Pairs after applying a debiasing method. Biased words associated with religion included 'greedy' for Jews, 'judgemental' for Christians, and 'violent'/'terrorist' for Muslims.
